one_month_reasoning: The window holds the Q3 FY27 print (quarter ended 2026-10-31), expected ~Wed 2026-12-02 after the close (not confirmed by the company [19,20]), so the 2026-12-03 close carries the earnings reaction. Expectation: another beat (10/10 product beats, median +4.6%; set 1,617.7 vs guide 1,588-1,593) with EPS ~0.65 vs Street 0.60 and whisper 0.71 (80% range 0.41-1.01): the whisper sits above our number, so a beat is largely priced. Industry read-across is supportive: hyperscaler consumption re-accelerated in CQ3 2026 (Azure +48% cc, Google Cloud +103% [25]) and Databricks grew >80% [24]; offsetting, Microsoft's database PAYG (up to 30%) and Fabric (up to 20%) discounts start 2026-11-02 [25] and a ~$286M note-repurchase loss may hit headline non-GAAP EPS (~-0.56) if not excluded. Distribution: lognormal around today's price with +1% median drift (post-beat drift, positive industry tape) and 19% monthly sd (64% realized / 3.5, a touch above for the print); no directional call beyond that.

downside.story: P10: the set's approved downside drivers (nrr -4 pt, new_cust -25%, product_gm -2 pt: Iceberg/managed-Iceberg storage lets compute leak to Databricks SQL ($1.5B run-rate, >100% growth), S3 Tables and BigQuery; Azure database/Fabric discounts of up to 30%/20% from 2026-11-02 pressure pricing; AI inference at lower margin) plus a de-rating of -4.5 turns of EV/NTM sales (to ~8.1x, MDB-like) and -45 turns of P/E (to ~43x, the peer median) as growth heads to the low 20s%.

base.story: Approved drivers: NRR 127-128% through FY28 fading to ~118% by FY30; product revenue +37%/+31%/+25% FY27-29; non-GAAP op margin 15.4% -> 19.4% (FY29); AI consumption offsets Iceberg leakage; exit 12.6x EV/NTM sales (k-rule on a 7.14x cleaned peer median) and 88x non-GAAP P/E; net cash 2.5B at the horizon.

upside.story: P90: the approved upside drivers (nrr +3 pt, new_cust +20%, product_gm +1 pt: AI consumption compounding as the hyperscaler AI cycle runs (Google Cloud +103%, Azure +48% in CQ3 2026) and Snowflake stays the governed-catalog layer over Iceberg) plus +4.0 turns of EV/NTM sales (to ~16.6x, above DDOG 15.2x, below NET 27.5x) and +40 turns of P/E (to ~128x).

Q2 FY27: (262.967) + 456.363 + 42.230 + 1.378 - 0.002 - 0.017 = 236.985 [6]. SBC is excluded from EBIT and recorded as its own quarterly line (sbc); FY26 SBC-related charges 36.5% of revenue. drivers.label: Net revenue retention rate (company definition: trailing-2-year cohort of capacity customers, product revenue year 2 / year 1; reported at quarter end)
drivers.source: Ex.99.1 'Financial Highlights' / Key Business Metrics: Q1 FY26 124%, Q2 125%, Q3 125%, Q4 125% [1-4], Q1 FY27 126% [5], Q2 FY27 126% [6] (10-Q: 126% at 2026-07-31 vs 125% at 2026-01-31 [7]); history Q4 FY24 131% [11], FY25 128/127/127/126% [12-15]. Definition: cohort = capacity customers using the platform in the first month of the first year of the trailing 2 years; NRR = cohort product revenue year 2 / year 1; churned customers count as zero [6].
drivers.derivation: Identity (per Kilian's spec): product revenue(q) = product revenue(same quarter a year earlier) x nrr + new_cust. Q3 FY27 128%, Q4 129%: the reported rate is trailing-12-month and lags the quarters (quarterly product growth 33.9%/36.8% in Q1/Q2 FY27 vs TTM product growth 31.1%/32.6% and NRR 126% [5,6]; the Q3 guide is +37-38% y/y [6]), so the TTM rate rises as H2 FY27 rolls in (CFO: third consecutive quarter of acceleration, existing-customer consumption is the driver [6,7]). FY28 129/127.5/126/124.5%: the AI step-up (CoCo 9,100 accounts, +2,000 in Q2 [6]) laps. FY29 123->120%, FY30 119->117%: the fade the company showed as the base grew (131% Q4 FY24 -> 124% Q1 FY26 [11,1]) plus Iceberg tables (storage and some compute outside Snowflake, 10-Q risk factor [7]), Databricks warehousing ($1.5B, >100% growth [23]) and price-performance cuts passed through. Check: the TTM residual implied by our quarters is 6.0% of TTM product revenue at Q4 FY27, 5.2% Q4 FY28, 3.9% Q4 FY29, 3.1% Q4 FY30 (FY25-FY26 actual 2.8-3.2%, Q2 FY27 5.0%): the FY28 reported rate could run ~1-2 pt above this path at the same revenue. Variant: downside -4 pt, upside +3 pt on every forecast quarter (scenarios).
drivers.why: The consumption metric the company and the Street use for existing-customer growth; the debated item (AI consumption up, Iceberg/storage and price cuts down).

drivers.label: Product revenue not explained by NRR: customers outside the NRR cohort (new logos of the last ~24 months, on-demand) + acquisitions ($M a quarter; identity residual)
drivers.derivation: Q3 FY27 135, Q4 110: the H1 FY27 residual (78, 118) is not all new-customer revenue: it holds the TTM lag of NRR (quarterly existing-customer growth runs ahead of the TTM rate) and Observe; as the TTM NRR catches up (128-129%) the residual falls back. FY28 80/72/68/66, FY29 66-70, FY30 70-74 = 2.3-3.0% of product revenue, the FY25-FY26 structural level (quarterly residual 1.4-4.9%, mean 2.9%; TTM 2.8-3.2%), growing slowly with net customer adds (616-740 a quarter [4,7,8]). Variant: downside -25%, upside +20%.
drivers.why: Keeps the NRR identity closed: every dollar of product revenue is either existing-cohort (nrr) or this residual; makes new-logo and acquisition revenue visible.

drivers.label: Non-GAAP product gross margin (non-GAAP product gross profit / product revenue, Ex.99.1)
drivers.source: Ex.99.1 reconciliation 'Non-GAAP product gross profit': Q1 FY26 754.124 / 996.813 = 75.7%, Q2 833.631 / 1,090.496 = 76.4%, Q3 879.165 / 1,158.377 = 75.9%, Q4 921.462 / 1,226.631 = 75.1% (FY26 3,388.382 / 4,472.317 = 75.8%) [1-4]; Q1 FY27 1,002.695 / 1,334.329 = 75.1%, Q2 FY27 1,114.084 / 1,491.861 = 74.7% [5,6]. Guide: FY27 non-GAAP product gross margin 75% (2026-02-25 [4]) cut to 74.0% (2026-09-02 [6]). 10-Q: GAAP product GM 71% vs 72%, 'costs attributable to newly launched product capabilities ... not yet reached economies of scale', partly offset by better cloud-infrastructure discounts [7].
drivers.derivation: FY27 guide 74.0% on product guide 6,070 [6] implies H2 GP 4,491.8 - H1 2,116.8 = 2,375 on H2 product 3,243.8 = 73.2%; the company beat its FY26 guide (75% -> 75.8%), so Q3 74.0%, Q4 73.5% (FY27 74.3%). FY28 73.5% flat: AI inference (Cortex, CoCo, Snowflake Intelligence) grows faster than core warehousing and carries third-party model and GPU costs; FY29 73.5-74.0%, FY30 74.0-74.5% as AI features scale and cloud discounts renew. Variant: downside -2 pt (AI mix at lower margin, hyperscaler pricing), upside +1 pt.
drivers.why: Makes AI gross-margin dilution visible; op margin = gross profit - opex is computed, not a driver.

drivers.label: Non-GAAP operating expenses (S&M + R&D + G&A) % of revenue (Ex.99.1)
drivers.derivation: Q3 FY27 54.5% (opex 923 = +5.8% q/q, as Q3 FY26 +5.8% [3]; revenue +9.5% q/q) -> op margin 16.8% vs guide 15.5% [6] (beat record median +3.0 pt, taken at +1.3 because the GM guide was cut); Q4 54.0%. FY28 55.5/53.5/53.0/52.5% (Q1 payroll-tax and merit reset: Q1 FY26 63.4% vs Q4 FY25 59.6% [1,15]); FY29 ~52.4%, FY30 ~51.0%: opex grows ~26% / 22% / 18% vs revenue ~30% / 24% / 20% (H1 FY27 opex +24% y/y vs revenue +34% [6]). Variant: opex grows with revenue from FY28 (FY30 op margin ~-4 pt).
